0-4776-1-1.subevent: A Bangladesh court sentenced 16 people to death for the murder of Nusrat Jahan Rafi, including the headteacher she had accused of sexual harassment.
Nusrat, 19, died in April after being set on fire in Feni for accusing her teacher of harassment; her murder sparked mass protests demanding justice.
The trial was one of the quickest in Bangladesh, concluding in 62 days, and the prosecutor said it proved that no one will get away with murder.
Nusrat's mother expressed ongoing pain upon hearing the verdict, and lawyers for the defendants announced they will appeal.

The investigation revealed a conspiracy involving classmates and local leaders; the headmaster ordered the killing from prison, and police collaborated by spreading false information that Nusrat had committed suicide.
Nusrat's family, who have police protection, welcomed the verdict but remain in fear for their lives, and her brother urged the prime minister to ensure their security.

On April 6, 11 days after reporting the headmaster, Nusrat was lured to her school's rooftop; when she refused to withdraw her complaint, she was set on fire by people in burqas; she escaped, gave a statement naming her attackers, and died four days later.

The case sparked nationwide protests and attention, with Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina pledging that none of the culprits would be spared; activists said the killing exposed a culture of impunity around sex crimes.

0-4731-3-t.subevent: More than 50,000 Americans died from drug overdoses last year, the most ever.
Heroin deaths rose 23 percent to 12,989, slightly higher than the number of gun homicides.
Deaths from synthetic opioids, including illicit fentanyl, rose 73 percent to 9,580.
Prescription painkillers killed 17,536, an increase of 4 percent.
Robert Anderson of the CDC said he had never seen anything like this in modern times.
Overall overdose deaths rose 11 percent to 52,404, while car crash deaths were 37,757 (up 12 percent) and gun deaths totaled 36,252 (up 7 percent).

The CDC found that rates for 8 of the 10 leading causes of death rose, causing life expectancy to drop for the first time in over 20 years, with drug overdoses and increased heart disease death rate as major factors.

17-26898-4-1.subevent: Chelsea announces Three as its new official shirt partner.
The partnership is initially for three years from the 2020/21 season, with Three's logo on all Chelsea shirts including men's, women's, and academy teams.
Three will make Stamford Bridge 5G-enabled within the first year of the partnership.
Chelsea CEO Guy Laurence states that Three is a natural partner due to the club's large social media following and digital engagement.
Three CEO Dave Dyson states that the partnership reflects shared values and covers the entire club, and that Three is building the UK's fastest 5G network.
The article notes that the partnership ends a five-year shirt sponsorship with Yokohama, but Yokohama continues as official tyre partner.
Three was launched 17 years ago as the UK's first 3G-only network and now has over 10 million customers.
Three's network covers 99% of the UK population and has won awards for data and roaming.

4-35859-4-1.subevent: A rabbi was wounded in a deadly shooting attack in Jerusalem; one person was killed and four wounded before officers shot and killed the terrorist, a Hamas member.
The rabbi says he was returning from morning prayers at the Western Wall wearing tefillin and tallit when the shooting started.
He felt a strong pain in his arm at the tefillin spot and turned back toward the Western Wall to find a building to enter.
He says he understands the miracle and that God did him a favor, and that tefillin are connected to the heart making him feel protected.
He does not know if the tefillin slowed the bullet.
Other wounded include a yeshiva student in serious condition and two police officers lightly hurt and released.

2-34418-4-t.subevent: Separatist rebels in Manipur banned Hindi movies and satellite TV channels in 2000 to protect Manipuri culture.
Cable operators filled the entertainment vacuum by introducing Korean channels such as Arirang TV and KBS World.
Shops in Imphal are packed with DVDs of South Korean films, TV soap operas, and CDs of Korean pop stars, especially boy bands.
Hairdressing salons display head shots of Korean celebrities and offer popular Korean-style haircuts.
Teenagers buy skinny jeans and other clothing trends inspired by Korean television shows at Gambhir Market.
Korean phrases like annyeong-haseyo (hello), kamsahamnida (thank you), and sarang-haeyo (I love you) have entered conversations in schoolyards and marketplaces.
Student Akshaya Longjam said she and her friends practice Korean phrases and talk about growing up in Korea, and she is a fan of Big Bang and G-Dragon.
College student Soma Lhishram said watching Korean soaps and films takes her away from daily problems like water and electricity shortages.
Research scholar Otojit Kshetrimayum said the key factor behind Korean pop culture's popularity in Manipur is cultural proximity in appearance and values.

0-4745-2-2.subevent: Emperor Naruhito formally proclaimed his ascension to the throne in an elaborate ceremony at the imperial palace.
He officially began his reign in May after his father Emperor Akihito abdicated due to poor health.
The ceremony took place as Japan dealt with the aftermath of Typhoon Hagibis, which left nearly 80 dead, and a parade was postponed.
During the ceremony, Naruhito read a formal proclamation from the Takamikura throne, dressed in a traditional garment.
Empress Masako sat in a separate smaller throne, and Prime Minister Abe delivered a congratulatory address followed by shouts of 'Banzai!'.
The ceremony featured ancient sacred treasures and was attended by hundreds of foreign dignitaries, including Prince Charles.
After the ceremony, Emperor Naruhito will host a tea party for foreign royalty, and Prime Minister Abe will host a banquet.
Small crowds gathered outside the palace despite rain, and some social media users reported a rainbow during the ceremony.

2-34088-2-t.subevent: The Pennsylvania grand jury released a report detailing child sex abuse by over 300 priests in six dioceses, involving at least 1,000 victims, and condemning the clerical culture that enabled it.
The report implicated church officials, including Archbishop Donald Wuerl, in a cover-up, and the Vatican condemned the acts while Pope Francis issued a personal apology.
The report raises the question of why it emerges 16 years after the initial 2002 Boston Globe exposé, which prompted the Dallas Charter reforms requiring clergy to report abuse to police.
Most of the Pennsylvania allegations are decades old, predating the Dallas Charter, and attorney Matt Haverstick noted that abuse cases have dropped significantly since the 1970s and 1980s.
David Gibson stated that the report is a vital historical record but should not be conflated with the church's current policies, which have been effective since the reforms.
The recent cases of Cardinal McCarrick and allegations in other countries, amplified by social media, have created a 'perfect storm' for renewed reckoning, according to Gibson.
The investigation originated from a 2015 lawsuit in Cambria County, expanded to two grand jury probes, and the church resisted publicizing findings, leading to partial redactions.
A key challenge remains addressing bishops who covered up abuse, as Dallas reforms lack protocols for them, and the ultimate lesson is the need for centralizing abuse narratives.

9-21221-2-1.subevent: Portugal's Catholic bishops announced the suspension of public Masses from Jan. 23 due to the extreme gravity of the coronavirus crisis.
Portugal is experiencing a surge in COVID-19 deaths, with 609,000 cases and 9,920 deaths recorded as of Jan. 22.
This is the second suspension of public worship by the bishops; the first was in March 2020 and was eased at the end of May.
The bishops said the suspension includes catechesis and other pastoral activities requiring gatherings, and called on priests to offer livestreamed Masses.
Earlier in January, the bishops called for the suspension or postponement of baptisms, confirmations, and marriages.
Funerals may be celebrated according to May 2020 norms requiring social distancing, and a Lenten retreat for the bishops has been canceled.
The Shrine of Our Lady of Fatima will broadcast three Masses and two rosaries daily during the suspension, with the rector expressing solidarity via television participation.

12-8952-1-5.subevent: Pope Francis held a special Urbi et Orbi blessing on Friday from the steps of St. Peter’s Basilica, an extraordinary event usually reserved for Christmas and Easter, due to the global Covid-19 pandemic.
Standing in a deserted St. Peter’s Square in the rain, he spoke to the world through modern communication media.
He prayed in the presence of the ancient icon of Mary Salus Populi Romani and the miraculous crucifix kept in the church of San Marcello.
He exposed the Blessed Sacrament for adoration and imparted his Apostolic Blessing, offering a plenary indulgence.
In his meditation, he reflected on the Gospel passage of Jesus calming the storm, saying the pandemic reminds us we are all in the same boat and calls us to cry out to Jesus.

He said the storm exposes our vulnerability and false certainties, revealing our common humanity, and noted that we have gone ahead ignoring wars and injustice, now it is a time of choosing what matters.
He praised those who gave their lives in service and said faith begins when we realize we need salvation; God turns everything to good.
He said Jesus' cross is our anchor and hope, and that He is risen and living by our side.
He concluded by entrusting everyone to the Lord through Mary's intercession, and giving a blessing that God may bless the world and give comfort.

17-27378-4-1.subevent: Darkside hackers were likely behind the ransomware attack that shut down the Colonial Pipeline.
Similar cyberattacks have occurred in Europe since 2014, culminating in the 2017 NotPetya attack.
The EU has strengthened its energy system resilience but the work is far from over.
Dutch MEP Bart Groothuis called for new regulation on critical infrastructure companies.

ENISA reported about 100 significant cybersecurity incidents in the energy sector in 2020, half ransomware, and energy operators face limited requirements under the NIS Directive, with SCADA systems most exposed.
The Colonial attack targeted business-side systems, not directly infrastructure, and the company is the first line of defense.

The EU requires member states to keep at least 90 days' worth of oil imports stocks, but Bulgaria, Romania, and the Czech Republic have repeatedly failed, and the crude pipeline network is less dense, with transport by truck/rail increasing flexibility.
Natural gas is a bigger worry; an October analysis simulated winter cutoffs on three Russian routes, concluding Romania could be stranded if the Ukrainian route is hit.
Sergiy Makogon urged energy diversification and warned of Nord Stream 2 risks, while ACER's Shortall said cyber threats require simulation and preventive strategies.

EU legislators are considering a strengthened NIS regime with fines up to 2% of turnover and network codes, and the sector shares information in a European Energy Information Sharing and Analysis Center.

3-17198-3-t.subevent: Last year more than 1 million refugees and migrants arrived in Europe.
The Trust Women conference will discuss solutions for tackling the crisis on Wednesday.
At the end of 2015 there were 65.3 million forcibly displaced people, more than half from Syria, Afghanistan, and Somalia.
Developing regions host 86 percent of refugees, with Turkey hosting the most and Lebanon having the highest concentration.
Nearly one in 200 children is a refugee, and the number has more than doubled; over 100,000 unaccompanied minors applied for asylum last year.
The U.N. refugee agency estimates more than 1.19 million people will need to be resettled next year.
Nearly 370,000 refugees and migrants have arrived in Europe this year by sea, mainly from Syria, Afghanistan, Nigeria, Pakistan, Iraq, and Eritrea.
After border closures and the EU-Turkey deal, numbers crossing from Turkey to Greece fell sharply, but more than 75,500 refugees are stranded in Greece and the Western Balkans.
At least 4,690 migrants have died in the Mediterranean this year while trying to reach Europe.

1-14865-1-1.subevent: Spitzer captured enough light from exoplanets to identify molecules in their atmospheres, a landmark achievement.
Spitzer obtained spectra for hot Jupiters HD 209458b and HD 189733b, revealing they are drier and cloudier than predicted, with hints of silicates.
Scientists Dr. Michael Werner and Dr. Jeremy Richardson expressed surprise at the unexpected results.
Two other teams led by Grillmair and Swain also captured spectra of these planets with similar findings.
Spectrum creation and that these are the first exoplanet spectra were explained.
Astronomers hope to obtain spectra of rocky planets to look for life; Swain called it a dress rehearsal.
Spitzer used the secondary eclipse technique and its spectrograph to isolate and obtain the planets' spectra.
Previous Hubble observations revealed elements at high altitude, supporting the presence of high clouds.
Astronomers plan further spectral studies of transiting exoplanets.

0-4736-3-2.subevent: Student Christopher Madrid was shot by army troops while protesting near the Catholic University in central Santiago, and he described being grazed by a bullet and seeing many people with head wounds.

The week-long uprising sent hundreds to hospitals with gunshot wounds and head fractures, left at least 19 dead nationwide, and forced hospital staff to work 24-hour shifts due to a strict military curfew.
President Sebastián Piñera declared that the authorities 'are at war' with protesters, but later announced a cabinet reshuffle and said he would ease the military-enforced curfew.

Posta Central health clinic lacked basic medical supplies such as surgical gloves, syringes, masks, and blood sample flasks, leading staff to cannibalize devices for trachea filters and causing at least one patient per week to die unnecessarily.

Health minister Jaime Mañalich mocked the upheaval on national TV and sabotaged attempts to record gunshot wounds, while Medical Association president Izkia Siches accused hospital directors of under-reporting injuries and demanded release of full figures.

Posta Central deputy director Luis Carrasco banned human rights observers from entering the facility and bought padlocks to further limit access; he had previously worked as head of surgery at the National Police Hospital.

Protesters continued to be shot and beaten: Camilo Rojas described being shot at and having his watch shattered; law students gathered statistics on victims including a journalism student beaten until she could not talk and a woman with a broken jaw from a rifle butt.
Chilean TV news broadcasts censored images of protests, leading to angry crowds surrounding stations; Televisión Nacional de Chile was forced to protect its headquarters with heavily armed soldiers.
A healthcare worker reported that many protesters were shot in the eye at Posta Central, resulting in shattered eyes and poor chances of regaining vision.

11-23312-2-4.subevent: A San Bernardino County medical examiner attributed Kimberly Gervais's Nov. 15 death to complications of spinal injuries suffered in the 2017 Las Vegas shooting.
The Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department stated it would not increase the official death toll, with spokesman Larry Hadfield saying the number is not going to change.
The shooting occurred on Oct. 1, 2017, at the Route 91 Harvest festival, killing 58 and injuring hundreds; the gunman killed himself and no motive was determined.
Gervais was left quadriplegic from a bullet that lodged in her vertebra and had shrapnel injuries; she was in and out of hospitals for two years.
Gervais's daughter Amber Manka expressed relief at the coroner's ruling and wanted her mother to be remembered but was cautious about harming other families.
The delay in the coroner's ruling was due to complications from other medical problems, according to investigator Sutcliffe.
Gervais attended the festival with friends; during the shooting, two men helped her, using a bandana to control bleeding and carrying her out.
Gervais spent two weeks in ICU and relied on a wheelchair afterward, but her daughter said she displayed superhuman strength.
Gervais was laid to rest in Malta Bend, Missouri.

0-4925-1-1.subevent: A bomb-laden motorbike exploded in Afghanistan's Kandahar province on Wednesday.
Seven civilians sustained injuries from the explosion.
The incident took place at 1:11 pm local time in the bazaar of Spin Boldak district.
The motorbike was parked in front of a hotel.
An investigation into the incident has been initiated.

2-wiki-img/34493-1/34493-1-1.subevent: Brazil's Central Bank sold US$1 billion to avoid a devaluation of the real.
After the rate swaps auction, the real closed 0.55% up at R$5.508 per dollar.
The BCB sold 20,000 currency swap contracts in an unscheduled auction, double the volume offered on Sept. 30.
Last month, the BCB announced it would hold additional auctions of traditional currency swaps twice a week.
Another sale worth US$1 billion was scheduled for Thursday morning to boost the local currency.
The real has lost a third of its value against the dollar in 2021 due to political risks, fragile economic recovery, and rising interest rates elsewhere.
BCB Director Fabio Kanczuk said the market reacted below expectations to the announcement of new regular swap auctions.

33-wiki-img/2481-1/2481-1-1.subevent: The official Pokémon Twitter account received angry fans, gameplay footage was downvoted, the Pokémon subreddit was full of concerned threads, and the hashtag #bringbacknationaldex trended.

Producer Junichi Masuda announced that only Pokémon from the Galar region will be available in Pokémon Sword and Shield, saying that the large number of existing Pokémon and the Switch's features made importing all monsters difficult and that they aimed for higher fidelity with higher quality animations.

Fans questioned Masuda's explanation about improved animations, pointing out that in-game battle animations have always been limited, and an increasingly convincing leak stated that the upcoming game would allow camping with Pokémon, which might require new animations.
Hackers claimed that the in-game models are being reused from previous games, which influenced the angry rhetoric even though it was difficult to confirm.

Players expressed attachment to their Pokémon collections, as the franchise's 'gotta catch 'em all' identity and the ability to transfer Pokémon from game to game had encouraged them to form bonds with their digital creatures.

Game Freak, the developers, encouraged hardcore players to pay for cloud storage to preserve their Pokémon for future games, so the inability to use transferred Pokémon in Sword and Shield felt like a slap in the face.

The backlash escalated as many fans called Game Freak 'lazy,' but the article argued that no such thing as a lazy game developer exists and that the issue was a difference in priorities, as Game Freak focused on other features like raids, an open world, and improved graphics.

Masuda stated that there are currently no plans to change the compendium via future updates, indicating that discourse about the missing National Dex would likely continue until the release of Sword and Shield.

1-15417-7-t.subevent: UW-Green Bay decided to teach classes via alternative delivery methods starting March 23.
Students leaving campus for spring break are asked to remain home until further notice and bring home all course material.
Campuses remain open and essential services are available; students unable to leave campus will be provided accommodations.
University-sponsored spring break trips for staff and faculty have been canceled.
All campus events from March 14-22 have been canceled and the Kress Events Center will be closed to the public from March 14-29.
Green Bay athletics will continue to monitor the situation with guidance from NIT, Horizon League, and NCAA.
A press conference is scheduled for 4 p.m. Wednesday to update the community.

3-16765-5-t.subevent: Italy's Economy Minister Roberto Gualtieri said the main business lobby's forecast of a 6% fall in GDP this year is realistic.
On Tuesday, national business association Confindustria said the outbreak would cause a serious recession in 2020.
Gualtieri told Il Fatto Quotidiano that the estimates are realistic and the Italian economy can aim at a vigorous rebound.
The government is scheduled to publish its own estimates in the Document of Economy and Finance (DEF) at the end of April.
Italy's output rose 0.3% last year, and the government expected it to grow 0.6% this year before the coronavirus emerged at the end of February.
At the end of March, two sources told Reuters that the Treasury expected the economy to contract around 3% this year.
Gualtieri said a new stimulus package, set to be approved this month, would be significantly larger than the 25 billion euros passed in March and sufficient for the entire epidemic.
He said the package would include an extension of state-backed guarantees for companies seeking liquidity, unemployment benefits, and support to people on low incomes.
Gualtieri said the use of the European Stability Mechanism (ESM) under current conditions was not an option.
He said Europe needed to coordinate a shared fiscal policy in addition to the European Central Bank's intervention.
He said new solutions are needed to grant parity of conditions and define an adequate shared and responsible response.

22-wiki-img/3685-3/3685-3-3.subevent: Marine Le Pen, an anti-immigration Eurosceptic, is expected to top the first round of France's presidential election.
Génération Identitaire (GI) specializes in publicity stunts to reclaim French territory from migrants, with 120,000 Facebook fans.
GI leader Pierre Larti debates a North African man, arguing against the replacement of Christian French values by Islamic ones.
GI is expanding across Europe, as identitarians see a continental battle between European and Islamic culture.
Jean-Yves Le Gallou's video 'Being European' gained over 3.2 million views, and his website Polemia represents the high-brow identitarian spectrum.
The website Fdesouche, a news aggregator chronicling migrant suburb chaos, receives about 3 million monthly views, surpassing Macron's site.
Alain Soral's website Égalité et Réconciliation has more readers than Fdesouche and is regularly prosecuted for incitement.
Eurosceptic students at Sciences Po set up a club 'Critique of European Reason', and after the Brexit vote they celebrated outside the UK embassy.
Students and young people report feelings of anti-white racism and cultural insecurity, with journalist Alexandre Devecchio calling them the 'Zemmour generation'.
The article notes that while Marine Le Pen's victory seems unlikely, polls have underestimated populist support before, and high abstention could help her.

0-4725-1-t.subevent: Marine archaeologists believe they have identified the wreck of the Japanese aircraft carrier Akagi, sunk during the Battle of Midway.
Researchers with the research vessel Petrel announced they had discovered the remains of two of the four Japanese carriers sunk during the battle within a week.
Expedition director Rob Kraft and historian Frank Thompson reviewed high-frequency sonar images and asserted that the dimensions and location indicate it is the carrier Akagi.
The Akagi was found in 5,490 meters of water, more than 1,300 miles northwest of Pearl Harbor.
Kraft described the wreck as sitting upright on its keel with visible bow, stern, gun emplacements, and part of the flight deck missing.
Thompson said seeing the wrecks is humbling and they are war graves.
The expedition is an effort launched by the late Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen, and the crew of the Petrel has found more than 30 vessels.

28-43-2-5.subevent: The Dutch Coast Guard reported that at least 21 containers washed ashore at the beaches of Vlieland, Terschelling, and Ameland, with more containers still in the water, and warned that three unlocalized containers could contain hazardous materials, advising against helping with cleaning.
Germany's Havariekommando updated that some containers have been spotted, including six in German waters, but it has not yet been determined if a container with dangerous goods was among those lost.
MSC announced it has started a clean-up operation and stated that a number of containers were damaged or lost overboard amid difficult conditions.
MSC stated it takes the incident very seriously and is collaborating with local authorities in all aspects of the clean-up.
MSC said it will ensure customers receive direct communications in the coming days and invited them to contact local representatives.
MSC appointed a salvage company to coordinate retrieval and beach clean-up, and deployed specialized ships equipped with sonar to search for missing cargo at sea.
MSC Zoe proceeded to Bremerhaven for cargo discharge operations and moored there at 00:35 after being accompanied by the multipurpose vessel Neuwerk.

0-4913-1-t.subevent: A plane made an emergency crash-landing in Ukraine on Wednesday, resulting in at least four deaths, according to Russian state-run RIA Novosti.
The AN-24 crashed in the Donetsk region with 45 people on board.
At least two people are unaccounted for.
Thirty-nine people were evacuated before the airliner caught fire.
An emergency official said the plane missed the landing strip, turned upside down and broke into pieces.
The charter flight was carrying soccer fans from Odessa to Donetsk for a UEFA Champions League game.

11-wiki-img/22287-3/22287-3-1.subevent: Malaysia arrested more than 4,000 people for violating lockdown orders.
Malaysia entered a 'harsh mode' of its Movement Control Order to enforce isolation.
Police set up hundreds of roadblocks, conducted inspections, and arrested thousands, including a man who jumped into the Strait of Malacca.
Senior Minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob announced the enforcement shift from soft to stern to harsh mode.
Malaysia reported 4,189 arrests for loitering, with 1,449 charged in court, while the Philippines reported over 20,000 arrests and President Duterte threatened to shoot violators.
Malaysia said its lockdown decreased COVID-19 spread, reporting 3,116 cases and 50 deaths, and Google data showed an 81% decrease in retail and recreation mobility.
Authorities arrested people for allegedly spreading misinformation about the virus, and human rights advocates warned of threats to free expression, with journalists self-censoring.
Digital strategist Jason Kelley of the Electronic Frontier Foundation warned that activists and free expression advocates are in danger when governments curtail speech during crises.
The political crisis following Mahathir Mohamad's failed power consolidation led to the old ruling party returning to power, complicating the pandemic response.
The government announced a $57.3 billion stimulus package called PRIHATIN, including cash aid, loans, deferred taxes, and debt payments.

11-wiki-img/22224-3/22224-3-1.subevent: Chief Minister Howard Quayle announces that from 15 June, outdoor gatherings of up to 30 people will be allowed, restaurants, pubs and cafés can serve diners indoors, gyms can partially reopen, and social distancing will be reduced to at least one metre.
The Isle of Man has no active cases of COVID-19, with 24 deaths linked to the virus.
Quayle says pubs will remain closed to drinkers and gyms must keep wet facilities like saunas shut.
Quayle praises the island's containment efforts, enabling boldness, and says it is time to accelerate towards the new Manx normal.
Quayle says the Council of Ministers is not ready to open the border to avoid risking achievements.

Health Minister David Ashford announces relaxed visiting restrictions at Noble's Hospital, allowing two visitors for compassionate grounds and one for all other wards, and says the government recognizes the crucial importance of support for patients.

3-17411-8-t.subevent: NOAA predicts an above-average Atlantic hurricane season with 13 to 20 named storms and up to five major hurricanes, and will update its forecast in August.
NOAA raised the definition of an average Atlantic hurricane season from 12 to 14 named storms.
There is a 60 percent chance 2021 will see an above-average hurricane season, the sixth in a row, and Colorado State University also predicted an above-average season.
Phil Klotzbach says the primary reasons are the low likelihood of El Niño and warm tropical Atlantic waters.
Without El Niño's wind shear, the Atlantic could see 6 to 10 hurricanes and 3 to 5 major storms.
Acting NOAA Administrator Benjamin Friedman urged preparedness during a press briefing.
The active 2020 season was due to La Niña which ended; the increased frequency of storms is not directly linked to climate change, but increased intensity is.
Matthew Rosencrans says most of the increase in storms is due to better technology, and NOAA uses hurricane hunters to measure storm conditions.
The National Hurricane Center monitored a possible first named storm northeast of Bermuda; the first named storm will be Ana and the second Bill.

2-34858-1-2.subevent: Expo 2020 Dubai recorded nearly 1.5 million visits in its first three weeks, which organizers credited to Space Week, a public holiday long weekend, and half-term school break.
Space Week featured debates on space commercialization, discussions on space debris and women in space, and activities like nebula music, star-gazing, and talks by UAE astronauts.
The Knights and Saudi Falcons aerobatic teams performed a show at the Expo site, and Al Wasl dome presented a space-themed projection show.
Children made up about a quarter of visits during the school break, attracted by cricket coaching by Rajasthan Royals, football sessions by Manchester City, and attractions at Al Forsan Park.
A spectacular opening ceremony on 30 September featured star-studded talent.

The recent long weekend saw large crowds at performances by Firdaus Orchestra (with A.R. Rahman), British singer-songwriter Sami Yusuf, and the start of Infinite Nights series with Kadim Al Sahir and Iyad Rimawi.
Popular regular events included the Kaleidoscope night-time light festival, the Expo 2020 Water Feature, the Garden in the Sky, and over 200 food and beverage outlets offering 50 global cuisines.
Virtual visitors rose to 10.8 million since 1 October, up from 9.3 million.
